title: Finite selection of polynomial-time word functions
statement: Let $f_0,\ldots,f_{r-1}$ be a finite list of polynomial-time computable functions from Boolean words to Boolean words. Suppose each function in the list is polynomial-time computable, and let $v$ be a function from Boolean words to $\mathbb{N}$ such that $z\mapsto 1^{v(z)}$ is polynomial-time computable. Then the function that, on input $z$, applies $f_{v(z)}$ to $z$ when $v(z)<r$, and returns the empty word when $v(z)\ge r$, is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $fs$ is a finite list of Boolean-word functions
Every function in $fs$ is polynomial-time computable
$v$ maps Boolean words to natural numbers
The unary word $1^{v(z)}$ is polynomial-time computable as a function of $z$
replaced: For a finite list of polynomial-time computable word functions and a polynomial-time unary selector, the function applying the selected list entry to the input, with the empty-word constant as out-of-range default, is polynomial-time computable; no unbounded transition table is consulted.
